s01.1.text: Every large language model is, at its core, a single mathematical function.

s01.2.text: It takes a sequence of tokens — and returns a probability for every possible next token.

s01.3.text: LLaMA-3-Lite is a compact, from-scratch implementation of Meta's LLaMA 3 architecture.

s01.4.text: Sixteen decoder blocks, a model dimension of one thousand twenty-four, and about five hundred fifteen million parameters.

s01.5.text: Let's open it up and follow one token all the way through.

s02.1.text: But before any mathematics can happen, text must become numbers.

s02.2.text: A tokenizer splits text into subword pieces from a vocabulary of one hundred twenty-eight thousand tokens.

s02.3.text: Each token ID indexes a row of the embedding matrix.

s02.4.text: That matrix holds one hundred twenty-eight thousand vectors, each one thousand twenty-four numbers long.

s02.5.text: That lookup places every token as a point in a high-dimensional space, where similar meanings sit close together.

s02.6.text: From here on, the model never sees characters again.

s03.1.text: These vectors flow through the network along a single channel: the residual stream.

s03.2.text: Each of the sixteen blocks reads from it, computes a transformation, and adds the result back.

s03.3.text: The stream is never overwritten, only refined, layer by layer.

s03.4.text: Each token's vector accumulates context, turning a bare lookup into a rich, position-aware representation.

s04.1.text: Inside each block, the first operation is normalization.

s04.2.text: As activations flow deeper, their scale can grow, and attention's dot products are sensitive to exactly that.

s04.3.text: RMSNorm measures a vector's root mean square, the square root of the average of its squared components.

s04.4.text: It divides that out, then rescales with a learned gamma.

s04.5.text: Unlike LayerNorm, there is no mean subtraction.

s04.6.text: Only the magnitude is regulated, which makes it cheaper, and just as stable.

s05.1.text: Now the heart of the model: self-attention.

s05.2.text: Every token's vector is projected three ways — into a query, a key, and a value.

s05.3.text: Each query takes a dot product against every key in the sequence, producing a score for every pair.

s05.4.text: Those scores are scaled by one over the square root of the key dimension.

s05.5.text: A causal mask hides the future: each token can look back at everything before it, never ahead.

s05.6.text: Then a softmax turns them into weights that sum to one.

s05.7.text: Finally, the weights blend the value vectors.

s05.8.text: Each output is a weighted average of what came before.

s05.9.text: And this runs not once, but eight times, in parallel heads with independent projections.

s05.10.text: Their outputs are concatenated and mixed by one last matrix.

s06.1.text: As defined, attention is order-blind — it sees a bag of tokens.

s06.3.text: Each head's query and key vectors are split into pairs.

s06.4.text: Each pair is rotated by an angle proportional to the token's position.

s06.5.text: The pairs rotate at different frequencies.

s06.6.text: Some spin fast, pinning down nearby positions; others barely move, encoding long-range structure.

s06.7.text: The elegance: a rotated query meeting a rotated key gives a special dot product.

s06.8.text: It depends only on the distance between the tokens, never on absolute position.

s06.9.text: With theta at five hundred thousand, the slowest pairs stay smooth across the entire two-thousand-forty-eight token context.

s07.2.text: LLaMA-3-Lite uses eight query heads but only four key-and-value heads.

s07.3.text: Each KV head is shared by two query heads.

s07.4.text: The KV cache stores keys and values for every layer and every past token.

s07.5.text: Halving the KV heads halves that memory, and the cache is what grows with context.

s07.6.text: And before rotation, queries and keys each pass through RMSNorm.

s07.7.text: It is called QK-norm, and it bounds their magnitude so logits stay well-behaved.

s07.8.text: A Lite addition — LLaMA 3 itself has none.

s08.1.text: After attention comes the second sublayer: a feed-forward network applied to each token independently.

s08.2.text: The vector is expanded to four thousand ninety-six dimensions, then compressed back to one thousand twenty-four.

s08.3.text: LLaMA uses a gated variant, SwiGLU.

s08.4.text: The expansion splits into two paths.

s08.5.text: One passes through the SiLU activation, a smooth ReLU.

s08.6.text: It gates the other path element by element, scaling each feature rather than switching it off.

s08.7.text: Then the result is projected back.

s09.1.text: Stack sixteen of these blocks, and the stream reaches a final RMSNorm.

s09.2.text: The output head scores every vocabulary item — a dot product against one hundred twenty-eight thousand embeddings, producing logits.

s09.3.text: A softmax turns them into probabilities.

s09.4.text: The model samples the next token and appends it.

s09.5.text: The whole network runs again — one forward pass per generated token.

s09.6.text: And that is the entire architecture: an embedding, a residual stream, and sixteen blocks.

s09.7.text: Normalized, rotary, grouped, gated computation, then an unembedding head.

s09.8.text: Five hundred fifteen million parameters — and nothing else.
